problem: Embodied AI rearrangement experiments are limited to ~100-200M steps because simulators like Habitat 2.0 (one process, one simulator, one environment; full rigid-body physics) run at only ~1.2k training SPS, so end-to-end RL for long-horizon mobile manipulation never converges (0% success reported in Habitat 2.0).
motivation: Scaling to billions of samples drove progress in CV/NLP and in PointNav (DD-PPO), but rearrangement training has stayed small because rendering, physics, inference and learning form a system where any bottleneck slows training. The authors observe that co-designing the whole rollout loop, and approximating physics kinematically, makes billions of steps feasible in days, letting a simple monolithic policy solve the task.
key_idea: Batch CPU-based kinematic physics together with GPU batch rendering (Bps3D) and PyTorch inference in a single process, so that simulation+RL reaches >100k SPS and end-to-end RL can be scaled to billions of steps.
insight: Throughput translates directly into capability: a plain ResNet18+LSTM policy trained with DD-PPO reaches 86.7% eval success at 5B steps, whereas the same policy in Habitat 2.0 gets 0% after 200M steps (it only learns to pick). The 15B-step run is still improving, so the task has not converged. Ablations show that learning stop/drop actions (79.63% vs 84.73%) and distractors (84.73% vs 99.5%) are what make the task hard, an analysis only possible when training to convergence.
method: Batched CPU physics: one C++ simulator instance in the main Python process steps 128 environments, sharing assets in memory, with zero-copy numpy buffers and reward/task logic in vectorized Python.
Batched GPU rendering: a single Bps3D renderer renders all environments' RGBD (128x128) and outputs a batch tensor consumed directly by PyTorch inference without copying to the CPU.
Pipelined rollout: physics runs in parallel with rendering and inference (one-step observation delay), so the rollout is GPU-bound and physics is effectively free.

Approximate kinematic simulation: base and joints are moved directly by offsets, collisions are tested with spheres (robot), oriented boxes (movable objects) and a 3 cm 'column grid' (static scene), with sliding resolved by heuristic jitter.

Kinematic suction grasp and snap-to-surface drop: a 3 cm sphere at the end effector attaches overlapping objects; on release the object is sphere-cast down and jittered up to 6 times to a collision-free resting position.

End-to-end RL training: a monolithic ResNet18 + 2-layer 512 LSTM policy trained with DD-PPO on 8 GPUs x 128 envs, with dense distance rewards, an action-smoothness penalty and a heuristic that only allows drop/stop near the goal.
Sim2sim transfer: the Galactic policy is used as a high-level 10Hz target joint-offset controller on top of a torque controller in Habitat 2.0.

setting.backbone: ResNet18 visual encoder + 2-layer LSTM (512) with actor/critic heads (trained from scratch with DD-PPO)
setting.training_data: RL in Galactic on 10k ReplicaCAD Rearrange Easy train episodes (63 layouts), 5B steps (46 h on 8 V100s); a 15B-step run also reported
setting.observation: 128x128 RGBD head camera (90° FoV) + joint proprioception + holding flag + base/end-effector relative position to object start and goal + step counter
setting.action_space: 11-dim continuous/discrete: base linear/angular velocity, 7 arm joint deltas, grasp/release, stop
setting.simulator: Galactic (new; Bps3D rendering + custom kinematic physics), ReplicaCAD; zero-shot transfer evaluated in Habitat 2.0
setting.privileged: 3D start and goal positions of the target object given as task specification (GeometricGoal); no map

numbers_note: Not a standard navigation benchmark. Throughput: 421,194 sim SPS and 108,806 training SPS on 8 V100 (14,807 train SPS on 1 V100), vs Habitat 2.0 1,243 training SPS. Mobile pick reaches 80% in 16 minutes vs >26 h (figure only). Rearrange (no heuristic) 79.63%, [No Distractors] 99.5% after 500M steps.
results: Galactic reaches 108,806 training SPS on 8 V100s (88x Habitat 2.0's 1,243) and 421,194 sim SPS. An end-to-end ResNet18+LSTM policy trained for 5B steps gets 86.70% eval success in Galactic, against 0% for Habitat 2.0 trained for ~200M steps, and transfers zero-shot to Habitat 2.0 at 26.40%. Mobile pick reaches 80% in 16 minutes vs >26 hours.
limitations: Approximate kinematic physics (snap-to-surface drops, sphere/column-grid collisions, sliding) gives a large sim2sim gap (86.7% to 26.4%) and no real-robot validation
Only GeometricGoal rearrangement with a Fetch robot in static ReplicaCAD scenes (no articulated furniture); policy relies on heuristics for stop/drop and on given 3D start/goal coordinates
Comparison with other simulators' SPS is loosely controlled, and the task remains unconverged even at 15B steps
